analysis.title: Risk Sentiment Recovers → Long MXN & DAX
key_insights: Midterm election results suggest Trump will have less room for political confrontation, which TS Lombard expects to lower geopolitical and trade uncertainty and lift risk sentiment.
Trade added: long DAX vs short XLP and XLU. Staples are at all-time highs while forward earnings growth rates are falling and revisions ratios are negative.
Utilities are exposed because slower US data-centre construction could curb AI electricity demand and weigh on sector revenue forecasts.

MXN has lost around 10% vs USD since the beginning of September. With risk sentiment recovering and Mexican growth accelerating, TS Lombard sees room for a rebound even though a dovish Banxico still weighs on the currency.
FX preference is long MXN vs CHF (lower safe-haven appeal) and vs CAD (weaker energy prices and already stretched near-term BoC tightening expectations).

On Iran, strategist Christopher Granville expects risk to tilt toward de-escalation even if the war returns to a kinetic phase, citing munitions shortages, casualty intolerance and midterm electoral pressure on Trump. Elevated oil prices look mostly like risk premia, since Persian Gulf flows remain close to pre-war levels.
Tech risk appetite has fallen close to Liberation Day levels on TS Lombard's measures, and the note argues it would not take much for it to recover.

Midterm results may impede new data-centre construction in states that just elected Democratic governors. TS Lombard still expects inference demand to keep rising on agentic tool adoption, with GPU rental prices rising across generations.
Rising GPU utilization and rental prices lead TS Lombard to conclude hyperscalers can still do well even if the AI infrastructure trade falters.

Portfolio update: closed long RSP vs XHB with a 3.6% loss because the expected more hawkish FOMC did not materialise. Short CHF/KRW hit its stop at +0.3% and is not re-entered given the slump in the AI infrastructure trade.

Retained long Canadian vs Japan 2y government bonds. The note says the market prices too aggressive a BoC path given Canadian economic weakness, while conditions for more BoJ hikes look good, with a terminal rate potentially above 2%.
